en: Theragāthā 16.1 Vīsatinipāta Paṭhamavagga (The First Chapter) [The verse of] Elder Sāriputta (Sāriputtattheragāthā) I have crossed over the flood; I am free from all bonds. Having abandoned all attachments, I dwell without clinging. My mind is well-liberated; I am cooled and at peace. I am a sage who has reached the end of the journey. I have no teacher; my like does not exist in the world. In this world with its devas, there is no one equal to me. I am the Worthy One (Arhat), the Fully Awakened One (Sammasambuddha); I alone am the unsurpassed teacher of devas and humans. I am the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Fully Awakened One. I am the Teacher of the world, including its devas. I am the One Who Has Reached the Ultimate Goal; I am the Knower of All Things, the All-Seeing. I have attained the destruction of all taints (āsava). I have lived the holy life; I have done what was to be done. There is no further state of existence for me. The Verses of the Elder Adhimutta:
“Those whom we formerly slew for the sake of sacrifice or for the sake of wealth;”
The rest are filled with fear,
trembling and lamenting; yet for you,
there is no state of fear.
Your complexion becomes even more serene;
why do you not lament in such a time of great terror?
“There is no mental suffering for one who is free from longing, O village headman;
all fears have been transcended.”
For one whose fetters are exhausted,
whose conduit to existence is destroyed,
who has seen the truth as it really is in this very life.
There is no fear of death for me,
as if laying down a burden;
my holy life has been well-practiced.
And the path has been well-cultivated;
I have no fear of death,
just as when diseases are destroyed.
The holy life has been well-practiced by me,
and the path too has been well-cultivated;
all states of existence have been seen as devoid of essence.
Like one who has drunk poison and vomited it up:
having reached the further shore, free from grasping,
his task accomplished and taintless.
He is content at the end of his life,
like one released from execution;
he has attained the supreme state of Dharma.
Having no concern for the whole world,
like one released from a burning house,
he does not grieve at death.
Whatever attachment there is,
or whatever state of existence can be found—
all this is without escape.
Thus it was said by the Great Seer:
"Whoever understands that in the manner taught by the Buddha,"
The Blessed One grasps at nothing,
like a red-hot iron ball;
he does not think, "I was."
‘I shall be’ does not occur to me;
conditioned phenomena will pass away—
what lamentation can there be in that?
For one who sees, as it truly is, the pure arising of phenomena and the pure continuity of conditioned formations,
There is no fear, O headman,
when one perceives with wisdom the world as being like grass and sticks.
Not finding anything to call "mine," he does not grieve, thinking, "It is not mine.
I am weary of this body.
I have no desire for existence;
this body will break apart,
and another shall not come to be.
Whatever you wish to do with this body,
do that as you desire; I have no concern for the consequences therein.
"Hatred and love shall arise.
Having heard those words of his—
wondrous and hair-raising—
Having laid aside their weapons,
the young men said this: "What,
venerable sir, have you done?"
Who is your teacher?
Having relied upon whose teaching is this state of sorrowlessness obtained?
“The All-Knowing, the All-Seeing,
the Victor, my Teacher;
the Greatly Compassionate One, the Master.”
The healer of the entire world.
Therefore, this Dhamma has been taught by him—
leading to the destruction [of suffering] and unsurpassed.
“By resorting to his teaching,
that state of sorrowlessness is obtained.
Having heard the well-spoken words of the Seer, the thieves—
Having laid aside their weapons and arms,
some desisted from that work,
while others took delight in going forth.
Having gone forth in the teaching of the Sugata,
those wise ones have developed the powers of the factors of enlightenment;
with uplifted minds, joyful, and with their faculties well-restrained, they dwell.
“They have entered the unconditioned state of Nibbāna.
… The Elder Adhimutta … [said this].
